newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament toughens traffic regulations.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament toughens traffic regulations.

text.p: Polish legislators approved a new tougher road traffic law on Friday to curb rampant car thefts and increase safety. Smoking or using a mobile phone at the wheel will now be an offence.
The bill, passed in a 311 to 19 vote with 20 abstentions, would create a central register of vehicles and drivers to which each police patrol car would have immediate access.

The new regulations, which will have to pass the Senate and be signed by the president, would gradually introduce new driving licences, car registration cards and plates to replace the current easy-to-forge ones.
Each vehicle would be required to have a special booklet in which all transactions regarding it would be marked.
"The final shape of the law can still be changed..., but clearly it should help us fight car thefts," police spokesman Andrzej Przemyski said.
There are more than 50,000 car thefts in Poland annualy and the number is rising. Poland is also a transit country for cars stolen in western Europe smuggled to Russia.
Transport Ministry spokeswoman Teresa Jarmolowicz said the central register for cars and driver would cost about 200 million zlotys ($65 million), which would be co-financed by insurance companies.
